# Regression models

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Regressor

`protocol Regressor` — A protocol for supervised regression models that predict continuous values. *(since 1.1.0)*

- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Predicts continuous target values for the given feature vectors. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per sample. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func predict(_ value: Double) -> Double` — Predicts a single target value from one single-feature sample. Returns: The predicted target value. *(since 1.1.0)*

## LinearRegression

`struct LinearRegression` — A trained ordinary least squares regression model.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Regressor.

- `let coefficients: [Double]` — The fitted coefficient vector.
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on.
- `let hasIntercept: Bool` — Whether this model includes an intercept (bias) term.
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double], intercept: Bool = true) throws -> LinearRegression` — Fits a linear regression model to the given training data. Returns: A trained `LinearRegression` model. Throws: `MatrixError.singular` if the features are linearly dependent.
- `static func fit(features: [Double], targets: [Double], intercept: Bool = true) throws -> LinearRegression` — Fits a linear regression model from a single feature array. Returns: A trained `LinearRegression` model with `featureCount` of 1. Throws: `MatrixError.singular` if the features are constant.
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Predicts target values for one or more samples. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per sample.
- `func predict(_ values: [Double]) -> [Double]` — Predicts target values for single-feature regression. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per input.
- `func summary(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double], level: Double = 0.95) throws -> RegressionSummary` — Builds a typed inference summary — coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, confidence intervals, R², adjusted R² — for the model evaluated on the training data that produced it. Returns: A typed `RegressionSummary` value. Throws: `MatrixError.singular` when `X'X` cannot be inverted. *(since 1.2.0)*

## Ridge.Outcome

`enum Outcome` — The outcome of the descent run that produced this model. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Hashable.

- `init?(rawValue: String)` *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case converged` — The convergence test fired within the iteration cap. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case maxIterationsReached` — The optimizer used every available iteration without satisfying the convergence test. The returned coefficients are the best-so-far estimate, not corrupted — but a tighter learning rate or a larger iteration cap would reach the minimum. Compare the first and last entries of `lossHistory` to confirm meaningful descent. *(since 1.3.0)*

## Ridge

`struct Ridge` — A regression model trained with an L2 (ridge) penalty on its coefficients. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Regressor.

- `let coefficients: [Double]` — The fitted coefficient vector. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on. Does not count the intercept term. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let hasIntercept: Bool` — Whether this model includes an intercept (bias) term. The intercept, when present, is never penalized. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let lambda: Double` — The L2 penalty strength used during fitting. Larger values shrink the coefficients harder; `0.0` recovers ordinary least squares. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let learningRate: Double` — The learning rate that was used during fitting. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let iterations: Int` — Number of iterations the optimizer used before stopping. Equal to `lossHistory.count − 1` because the trajectory begins with the loss at the initial all-zeros parameters. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let finalLoss: Double` — The final penalized-loss value at the returned coefficients. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let lossHistory: [Double]` — The full loss trajectory of the penalized objective, beginning with the loss at θ = 0 and ending with `finalLoss`. Length is `iterations + 1`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let outcome: Outcome` — Whether the run converged or hit the iteration cap. See `Outcome`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double], lambda: Double, learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> Ridge` — Fits a ridge regression model to the given training data. Returns: A trained `Ridge` model. Throws: `divergedNonFinite(iteration:loss:)` when the iterate produces a `NaN` or `±∞` loss; `divergedIncreasing(iteration:previousLoss:currentLoss:)` when the penalized loss strictly increases beyond the tolerance. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [Double], targets: [Double], lambda: Double, learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> Ridge` — Fits a ridge regression model from a single feature array. Returns: A trained `Ridge` model with `featureCount` of 1. Throws: `GradientDescentError` on divergence. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Predicts target values for one or more samples. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per sample. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func predict(_ values: [Double]) -> [Double]` — Predicts target values for single-feature regression. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per input. *(since 1.3.0)*

`enum Outcome` — The outcome of the descent run that produced this model. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Hashable.

- `init?(rawValue: String)` *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case converged` — The convergence test fired within the iteration cap. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case maxIterationsReached` — The optimizer used every available iteration without satisfying the convergence test. The returned coefficients are the best-so-far estimate, not corrupted — but a tighter learning rate or a larger iteration cap would reach the minimum. *(since 1.3.0)*

## GradientDescent

`struct GradientDescent` — A regression model trained by batch gradient descent, and the shared optimizer behind every iterative model in Quiver. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Regressor.

- `let coefficients: [Double]` — The fitted coefficient vector. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on. Does not count the intercept term. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let hasIntercept: Bool` — Whether this model includes an intercept (bias) term. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let learningRate: Double` — The learning rate that was used during fitting. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let iterations: Int` — Number of iterations the optimizer used before stopping. Equal to `lossHistory.count − 1` because the trajectory begins with the loss at the initial all-zeros parameters. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let finalLoss: Double` — The final loss value at the returned coefficients. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let lossHistory: [Double]` — The full loss trajectory, beginning with the loss at θ = 0 and ending with `finalLoss`. Length is `iterations + 1`. Inspecting this array is the canonical way to see whether descent was smooth, oscillated, or crawled — the diagnostic that turns `GradientDescent` from a black box into an observable process. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let outcome: Outcome` — Whether the run converged or hit the iteration cap. See `Outcome`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double], learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> GradientDescent` — Fits a gradient descent regression model to the given training data. Returns: A trained `GradientDescent` model. Throws: `divergedNonFinite(iteration:loss:)` when the iterate produces a `NaN` or `±∞` loss; `divergedIncreasing(iteration:previousLoss:currentLoss:)` when the loss strictly increases between iterations beyond the tolerance. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [Double], targets: [Double], learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> GradientDescent` — Fits a gradient descent regression model from a single feature array. Returns: A trained `GradientDescent` model with `featureCount` of 1. Throws: `GradientDescentError` on divergence. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Predicts target values for one or more samples. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per sample. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func predict(_ values: [Double]) -> [Double]` — Predicts target values for single-feature regression. Returns: An array of predicted values, one per input. *(since 1.3.0)*

## GradientDescentError

`enum GradientDescentError` — Errors thrown by `GradientDescent` when the optimizer cannot return a trustworthy result. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Equatable, Error.

- `case divergedNonFinite(iteration: Int, loss: Double)` — The iterate produced a non-finite loss (`NaN` or `±∞`) at the given iteration. Typically caused by a learning rate that is too large for the feature scale — the parameters overshoot, the predictions blow up, and the squared residuals overflow. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case divergedIncreasing(iteration: Int, previousLoss: Double, currentLoss: Double)` — The loss strictly increased between two consecutive iterations by more than one tolerance unit. The descent step overshot the minimum without yet producing non-finite values. Recovering would require a smaller learning rate or scaled features. *(since 1.3.0)*

## ResidualModel

`struct ResidualModel<Model> where Model : Regressor, Model : Decodable, Model : Encodable, Model : Equatable, Model : Sendable` — Pairs a fitted regression model with the residuals it leaves behind. *(since 1.4.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let model: Model` — The fitted regression model whose predictions define the expectation. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `init(model: Model)` — Wraps an already-fitted regressor. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func expected(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — The expected values the wrapped model predicts for the given features. Returns: One predicted value per sample. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func residuals(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double]) -> [Double]` — The residuals `observed − predicted`, one per sample. Returns: One residual per sample, `targets[i] − predicted[i]`. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func residual(features: [Double], observed: Double) -> Double` — The residual for a single observed value at one sample. Returns: `observed − predicted` for the single sample. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `var coefficients: [Double] { get }` *(since 1.4.0)*

## Coefficients

`protocol Coefficients` — A model you can read the numbers out of. *(since 1.4.0)*

- `var coefficients: [Double] { get }` — The model's learned numbers: the base value (intercept) first, then one weight per input, in the order the inputs were given. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func equation() -> String` — Renders the fit as a readable equation, such as `y = 38000.00 + 110.00x`. Returns: The fitted formula as a string. An empty coefficient vector renders as `y = 0`. *(since 1.5.0)*
- `func equation(variables: [String], response: String = "y") -> String` — Renders the fit as a readable equation with each variable named, such as `price = 38000.00 + 110.00·sqft`. Returns: The fitted formula as a string. An empty coefficient vector renders as `response = 0`. *(since 1.6.0)*

## ConfidenceInterval

`struct ConfidenceInterval` — A confidence interval for a single regression coefficient. *(since 1.2.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let lower: Double` — The lower bound of the interval. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let upper: Double` — The upper bound of the interval. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `init(lower: Double, upper: Double)` *(since 1.2.0)*

## RegressionSummary

`struct RegressionSummary` — A frozen snapshot of inference statistics for a fitted `LinearRegression`. *(since 1.2.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let coefficients: [Double]` — The fitted coefficient vector. When the model has an intercept the first element is the intercept; the remainder are feature weights. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let standardErrors: [Double]` — One standard error per coefficient. Same length and ordering as `coefficients`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let tStatistics: [Double]` — One t-statistic per coefficient. Equal to `coefficient / standardError`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let pValues: [Double]` — One two-tailed p-value per coefficient. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let confidenceIntervals: [ConfidenceInterval]` — One confidence interval per coefficient at the level specified when the summary was built (default 95%). *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let rSquared: Double` — The coefficient of determination, `R² = 1 - SS_res / SS_tot`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let adjustedRSquared: Double` — The adjusted coefficient of determination, `1 - (1 - R²) · (n - 1) / (n - p)` where `p` is the number of fitted coefficients (intercept counts when present in this convention). *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let n: Int` — The sample size — number of training rows. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let degreesOfFreedom: Int` — The residual degrees of freedom, `n - p`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let residualStandardError: Double` — The residual standard error, `sqrt(SS_res / df)`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let confidenceLevel: Double` — The confidence level used to compute `confidenceIntervals`, in `(0, 1)`. The default is `0.95`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `init(coefficients: [Double], standardErrors: [Double], tStatistics: [Double], pValues: [Double], confidenceIntervals: [ConfidenceInterval], rSquared: Double, adjustedRSquared: Double, n: Int, degreesOfFreedom: Int, residualStandardError: Double, confidenceLevel: Double)` *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func markdownTable() -> String` — Renders the summary as a Markdown table — one row per coefficient, plus a header line carrying R² and the residual standard error. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func csvRows() -> String` — Renders the summary as CSV — one row per coefficient. *(since 1.2.0)*
